title: Control Board Failure
shortDescription: The Electronic Oven Control has detected an internal self-check failure on the cooktop section.
fullDescription:
Kenmore cooktops (many made by Whirlpool or Frigidaire platforms) show F1 when the control ROM or RAM self-test fails. The cooktop usually beeps continuously and disables all surface elements.

Often a power surge or a shorted touch panel triggers F1. Disconnect briefly and see if it clears; if not the control board must be replaced.

causes.cause: Stuck touch key causing watchdog reset

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 5 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: If F1 returns, replace the electronic control board.

whenToCallPro: If power cycling does not clear F1 and you are not confident replacing boards.

faq.a: Most often yes, but always try a power reset first in case of a glitch.

title: Overheat at Control
shortDescription: Temperature near the cooktop control has exceeded safe limits.
fullDescription:
F2 appears when the control-area thermistor detects excessive heat, which can happen if ventilation is blocked or a hot pan has been left too close to the touch area on radiant models.

Let the cooktop cool fully, then check clearances and airflow under the unit.

fixSteps.title: Cool
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and let the cooktop cool for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Check clearance
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure required air gap below the cooktop is not blocked.

whenToCallPro: If F2 returns despite adequate ventilation, the thermistor or board need checking.

faq.a: Leave the manufacturer-specified gap below and behind the cooktop and avoid blocking any vent cuts.

title: Element Sensor Open
shortDescription: A surface element temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
Higher-end radiant Kenmore cooktops include limiter sensors under each element. F3 means one of those sensors is reading infinite resistance.

The fix is to replace the limiter assembly for the affected element, which requires removing the cooktop glass.

fixSteps.title: Identify element
fixSteps.instruction: Determine which zone reports F3; often shown with the element number.

fixSteps.title: Replace limiter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove glass and swap the limiter assembly for that element.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable removing the glass top.

faq.q: Can I use the other elements?
faq.a: Some models lock out the whole cooktop, others leave working elements available.

title: Element Sensor Shorted
shortDescription: An element limiter sensor is reading shorted.
fullDescription:
F4 is the short-circuit counterpart to F3. The limiter thermistor is reading near zero resistance, which would otherwise let the element run without temperature protection.

As with F3, the remedy is replacing the limiter assembly.

fixSteps.title: Replace limiter
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the limiter for the affected element.

whenToCallPro: If harness routing is unclear or glass removal is intimidating.

faq.a: Never - it is a safety device that prevents element overheating and fire.

title: Relay Board Failure
shortDescription: The relay board is not switching elements as commanded.
fullDescription:
Some Kenmore cooktops have a separate relay board stacked below the control. F5 is posted when command and feedback disagree, usually because a relay has welded closed or is not energising.

The relay board must be replaced; individual relays are rarely field-serviceable.
symptoms: Element stays on or never heats

fixSteps.title: Isolate power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker and verify with a voltmeter.

fixSteps.title: Replace relay board
fixSteps.instruction: Access and swap the relay board assembly.

whenToCallPro: A welded relay can leave elements live even when off - call a pro if unsure.

faq.a: A stuck-on element is dangerous. Leave the breaker off until repair is complete.

title: Line Frequency Error
shortDescription: The control cannot detect a stable 60 Hz supply.
fullDescription:
F6 indicates that the zero-cross detection circuit is not seeing a proper 60 Hz AC waveform. On a generator or inverter with poor waveform, or with a damaged neutral, this can appear. It can also indicate a failing control board.

Have the supply verified before replacing the board.

fixSteps.title: Verify supply
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage and frequency at the cooktop terminals.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If supply is clean, replace the control board.

whenToCallPro: Any suspicion of a wiring or supply issue.

faq.q: Can I run this on an inverter?
faq.a: Only a true-sine inverter with stable frequency will work reliably.

title: Stuck Touch Key
shortDescription: A touch key has been detected as pressed for too long.
fullDescription:
F7 is triggered when a capacitive touch key reads active for more than about 60 seconds. Liquid, food, or a cracked glass overlay are the most common causes.

Clean the surface thoroughly and power cycle. If the fault returns, the touch overlay or control board is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe touch area dry with microfibre cloth.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off for 2 minutes then restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: If F7 returns, replace the control board.

whenToCallPro: If glass is cracked or replacement is required.

faq.q: Does a child lock cause F7?
faq.a: No, child lock disables keys without reporting an error.

title: Overvoltage
shortDescription: Supply voltage is higher than the control board tolerates.
fullDescription:
F8 indicates that the control has measured supply voltage significantly above 240 V. A lost neutral in a split-phase home will easily cause this and will also damage other appliances.

Turn the breaker off immediately and have an electrician investigate before continuing.
whenToCallPro: Always - overvoltage is a safety issue.

faq.a: Possibly; check all functions after the supply is restored.

title: Door or Lock Circuit Error
shortDescription: On modular cooktop/oven combos, the oven door lock reports a fault.
fullDescription:
Some Kenmore drop-in units share the control with the oven. F9 on these can surface at the cooktop display when the oven door lock motor fails or the lock switch is miswired.

If you have a standalone cooktop with no oven, F9 typically means a main control fault.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off for 5 minutes and retry.

fixSteps.title: Replace lock or board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the lock motor or control board as diagnosed.

whenToCallPro: If door is locked closed with hot contents, call service immediately.

faq.a: No - you can damage the lock assembly. Call service to unlock safely.

title: Runaway Temperature
shortDescription: An element or bake circuit is running hotter than commanded.
fullDescription:
F10 is a safety trip when the control detects rising temperature with the element relay commanded off, usually from a welded element relay or shorted sensor reading cold.

Turn the breaker off promptly to prevent continued heating and call for service.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Have a technician diagnose relay and sensor circuits.

whenToCallPro: Always - runaway heating is a fire hazard.

faq.a: It can be; check your warranty before paying for repair out of pocket.
